messages:
marta (solutions): quick heads-up — FinSecure POC hitting intermittent streaming failures behind their corporate proxy. customer sees socket hang ups + 502/504s and occasional 429s when we retry. they use node TS sdk (node 18) and a corporate forward proxy (Zscaler-like).

alex (sales): ugh. any reproducible logs or request ids? are they streaming or non-streaming?

marta (solutions): streaming. attached log excerpt from their app: 

ben (eng-infra): paste logs here and we'll triage. also did they say if proxy terminates TLS or does CONNECT tunneling? that matters for http2.

marta (solutions): log snippet they sent: 
```
[FinSecure] 2026-03-20T17:05:12Z ERROR stream failed: ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR code=NGHTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR requestId=rq_0a1b2c3d
[FinSecure] 2026-03-20T17:05:12Z WARN retrying request attempt=1 after 120ms
[FinSecure] 2026-03-20T17:05:14Z ERROR socket hang up during data frame write
[FinSecure] 2026-03-20T17:06:02Z ERROR http status=504 upstream_response_time=58.2s requestId=rq_0a1b2c3d
```

luis (sdks): thanks — this reads like two overlapping issues: 1) http/2 + proxy interception causing NGHTTP2 protocol errors; 2) proxy session timeouts when long-lived streaming due to too many parallel sockets or missing keepalive. common with corporate interceptors that reframe streams.

ben (eng-infra): can they try forcing HTTP/1.1 for streaming? many proxies don't handle http2 proxying well. also ensure socket keepalive and lower connection pool size so the proxy doesn't drop idle sessions.

marta (solutions): customer asked for exact config to try. can we give quick Node and curl repros?

luis (sdks): suggested Node snippet: 
```
// node example (ts)
import { Redwood } from '@redwoodai/sdk';
import HttpsProxyAgent from 'https-proxy-agent';

const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent({
  keepAlive: true,
  maxSockets: 8, // fewer concurrent sockets helps corporate proxies
  timeout: 60000,
});

const client = new Redwood({
  agent,
  timeoutMs: 120000,
  maxRetries: 3,
  // force http/1.1 to avoid http2 proxy issues
  forceHttp1: true,
});

await client.stream({ model: 'gpt-open-2', input: 'hello' });
```

Also quick curl repro (ask them to run from a machine behind the proxy):
```
curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:8080 --no-http2 \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-open-2' \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

ben (eng-infra): add to that: if the proxy is re-signing TLS (MITM), ensure the client trusts the proxy CA OR use CONNECT tunneling. If MITM, streaming chunk boundaries can be mangled.

luis (sdks): also enable SDK debug log and capture request ids: set env DEBUG=redwood:sdk or use REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1. ask them to share the X-Request-Id that the SDK logs. we can correlate with ingress logs.

marta (solutions): they ran the curl with --no-http2 and saw fewer NGHTTP2 errors; still saw occasional long polls that ended with 504 after 60s.

ben (eng-infra): that 504 suggests proxy idle timeout. ask them to set keepalive pings from their side or reduce the maximum idle time on proxy. short term: reduce chunk interval or send small heartbeats from client to keep session active. also try lowering concurrency so the proxy doesn't hit connection limits.

luis (sdks): we can add a small client-side heartbeat option in SDK like streamKeepAliveMs: 15000 to send empty comments between chunks for the POC. for now, a shim: send a small prompt piece every 10–15s to keep connection alive.

marta (solutions): excellent. i'll pass Node snippet + curl + debug env to FinSecure. they also asked about retries/backoff — they saw our SDK retrying and then hitting 429s from the proxy. any advice?

ben (eng-infra): retries + proxy can amplify load. set maxRetries=2 with exponential backoff + jitter. and add an upstream circuit breaker so we don’t open many concurrent retries.

luis (sdks): sample retry policy in SDK config: { maxRetries: 2, baseDelayMs: 200, maxDelayMs: 2000, jitter: true } — we'll send them a snippet. Also recommend enabling idempotency for non-streamed calls.

marta (solutions): quick non-technical asks from customer: 1) can we provide a temporary Dedicated trial to avoid proxy issues during PoC? 2) they need SOC2 questionnaire answers.

alex (sales): Dedicated trial — we can offer a 30-day eval pool for enterprise POC. i'll start contract/credits discussion. security questionnaire — @security-bot can you pick this up?

security-bot: Thanks — forwarding SOC2 / security pack to FinSecure. will run through the questionnaire and ping if we need infra logs. ETA EOD tomorrow.

ben (eng-infra): if we spin up a Dedicated pool in their cloud region we can avoid the customer's proxy entirely for the streaming path (network topology permitting). for triage it's worth offering that as an option.

marta (solutions): plan I will follow: 1) send Node + curl repro + debug env to FinSecure and ask for X-Request-Id examples 2) suggest immediate config changes (force http1, keepAlive agent, reduce pool size, retry tuning) 3) offer Dedicated trial to rule out proxy 4) security team will handle SOC2 questionnaire.

alex (sales): perfect. cc'ing legal for credits. thumbs up once you have their logs and request ids and we'll escalate to eng to look at ingress traces. :thumbsup:

marta (solutions): thanks all — i'll update thread with their logs after they run curl.

luis (sdks): if they still see NGHTTP2 errors after forcing http1, send the SDK debug output and we'll triage client-side parsing.

ben (eng-infra): and if needed we can provision a short-lived Dedicated instance tied to the POC so they can verify behavior without proxy interference.

marta (solutions): noted — closing loop after the customer runs tests. thanks! :raised_hands:
